chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about a female slave of a people who came to a tribe other than her own tribe and informed them that she was free, and a man from them married her and she bore him children. He said: 'Her children are slaves, unless she produces evidence that two witnesses testified for her that she was free, then her children are not enslaved and they become free.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of children born to a female slave who claims freedom and marries?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *al-awlā li-l-ʿabd* (the slave takes precedence) in cases of disputed lineage, establishing that the default status of children follows the mother unless her freedom is proven. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preserving the status quo (*istishab*) while allowing for the elevation of status through valid testimony (*bayyina*), ensuring that the uncertainty of slavery is not imposed without clear evidence. The hadith underscores the importance of evidentiary standards in personal status law, reflecting the broader Islamic legal maxim that doubt is resolved in favor of the established state.
